newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Queensland projects A$13.6 mln 97/98 surplus.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Queensland projects A$13.6 mln 97/98 surplus.

text.p: The Australian state of Queensland on Tuesday projected an underlying budget surplus of A$13.6 million for 1997/98 (July/June), up from an estimated A$10.9 million in 1996/97.
The headline deficit was projected at A$99 million, down from the 1996/97 estimate of a A$567 million surplus, largely due to spending on capital works, the government said.

"The overall deficit for the state government in 1997/98 is a direct consequence of a significantly expanded capital programme funded from one off sources, and does not reflect an underlying deterioration in the State's financial position," the
A total of A$4.25 billion in capital outlays is planned, representing a 10.9 percent increase on 1996/97.
The underlying figure is derived on a consolidated funds (CF) basis, while the headline figure is derived on a government finance statistics (GFS) basis.
The GFS measure is broader in scope the CF measure as it measures the net accumulation or depletion of financial assets.
"It therefore represents the amount of funds which the government makes available to/requires from financial markets," the budget papers said.
Asset sales in the year are expected to total A$239 million, the bulk of which is made up of A$43.3 million from the sale of government property and A$124.6 million from the sale of freeehold land.
Treasurer Joan Sheldon said the budget was one which delivered for Queenslanders and was a logical progression from the conservative coalition's budget of last year.
Sheldon said the top priority of the government was jobs.
She forecast economic growth for the state at 4.5 percent in 1997/98, well above the national forecast of 3.75 percent.
The budget contained no new taxes or charges, or increased taxes or charges, she said.
